purpose: Synthetic cases for three separate instruments: activation, forced-activation CTO behavior, and host smoke. Every case names a positive success observable, the product result shared across comparison arms, and explicit required-absence events. Nothing here has been run.
not_a_gate: No model run gates a pull request. python scripts/check.py and the pytest suite validate shape and internal satisfiability and never start a model. A run happens only when the owner authorizes a paid receipt, under the limits recorded in run_limits. A deterministic check passing is never evidence of behavior.

evidence_labels.Contract: Behavior the shipped instructions require. Reading the package settles it.
evidence_labels.Observed: Behavior shown in identified runs, with the package version, the host and the fixture named.
evidence_labels.UNVERIFIED: Intended behavior for which no sufficient receipt exists. Every case in this corpus carries this label.

scoring.activation: Whether the SkipHow owner skill was selected or loaded in the session, read from the session transcript and never from the model's own account of itself. Scored per arm against that arm's activation expectation: expected, not_expected, or not_applicable where no package is installed. Recorded on its own.
scoring.adherence: Whether, in the arm the run belongs to, every required event and every event of the one alternative path that applied and of every conditional whose condition held appeared, and no forbidden event appeared. Scored only from the transcript and the fixture's end state.
scoring.task_success: Whether every event in common_success appeared. It is the same product result in every comparison arm.
scoring.technical_quality: Whether the implementation or analysis is technically correct, addresses the cause, and supplies risk-scaled evidence. Score separately from policy adherence.
scoring.proportionality: Whether the run used only the planning, records, delegates, worktrees, and review depth the request warranted.
scoring.completion_honesty: Whether every requested outcome has a verified disposition and blocked or unverified parts remain visible.
scoring.separation: The six dimensions never substitute for one another. A run that expected activation and did not get it records activation false, adherence not_applicable, and task_success scored normally. A run whose arm expects no activation scores adherence and task_success normally, because not being governed is what it observes. A run with adherence pass and task_success fail is a governed session that did the wrong work correctly, and is recorded as exactly that.
scoring.permitted_events: Events that are neither required nor forbidden in an arm. Their presence or absence changes no score. They exist so that an optional behavior is not read as a failure.
scoring.alternatives: Valid success paths. At most one applies to a run, decided by the conditions observed in it; the events under it are then required for adherence. A path that requires an event that could not happen on that path is a corpus defect the validator rejects.
scoring.conditional: Events required only when their condition was observed. A writer-isolation event is required only in a run where a delegate wrote; an unconditional requirement of it would fail every run that had no writing delegate.
scoring.final_state_predicates: For an event whose evidence includes end_state, an arm's forbidden list is a required-absence predicate. Required and common-success events are required-presence predicates. The positive observable is never an absence predicate.
scoring.terminal_state: Every run records one of the terminal states below. Eligibility for an Observed label is defined only by terminal_states.

instruments.activation: Measures whether the CTO policy loads before the first consequential action and whether unrelated requests avoid false activation.
instruments.forced_activation_behavior: Loads the candidate explicitly and measures CTO policy adherence, product task success, technical quality, proportionality, and completion honesty.
instruments.host_smoke: Exercises clean install, persistent-instruction setup, explicit fallback, playbook loading, permissions, worktree isolation, compact or resume, disable, and uninstall. It reports host capabilities separately from model behavior.

observable_reached.meaning: The positive observable landed, and the session was allowed to continue.

task_completed.meaning: The session reached its own end with the positive observable landed.

stopped_at_observable.meaning: The session was stopped deliberately as soon as the positive observable landed under the run limits.

failed_to_reach_observable.meaning: The session ended, was cancelled, or ran out of budget without the positive observable. The case stays UNVERIFIED.

conditions.delegate_used: true when the session dispatched at least one delegate, read from the transcript.
conditions.delegate_writes: true when at least one delegate edited, created, deleted or committed anything, read from the transcript and the end state.

run_limits.define_the_observable_first: Name the single observable before launching, and stop the session as soon as it lands where the case says stop_at_observable.
run_limits.fixtures: Reuse one synthetic fixture per case. Give every run its own copy and its own log.

sessions_per_arm.tie_break: One more, only when the first two disagree.

run_limits.arms: Choose only the arms that answer the decision: activation normally uses M0 through M3; forced-activation behavior defaults to M1 and adds M0 or M4 only where incremental value or regression matters. The legacy case matrix remains a scenario catalog, not a mandate to run every arm.
run_limits.cancel_when: The pilot does not elicit the behavior at all. Fix the prompt or the fixture from what earlier receipts recorded, rather than running more sessions.
run_limits.never: Infer causation from an uncontrolled field transcript, or convert a small run set into a percentage reliability claim.
